source.title: Generanno: A Genomic Foundation Model for Metagenomic Annotation
source.authors: Qiu-Yi Li; Wei Wu; Yiheng Zhu; Fu-Li Feng; Jie-Ping Ye; Zheng Wang

record.tranche_reason: The authors explicitly say Generanno's results defy conventional scaling laws and compare downstream task scores for models with different parameter counts. This is a limited challenge to downstream predictability, not a test of language-model loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation, or optimize parameters and tokens under a fixed compute budget. It reports downstream benchmark scores for models of different sizes and explicitly characterizes Generanno's performance relative to a larger model as defying conventional scaling laws. Results cited from other work about protein models are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper builds and benchmarks a 500M genomic DNA encoder. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit scaling curves or run a matched size sweep. Its 'defies conventional scaling laws' remark rests on a cross-family comparison: Generanno 500M versus GenomeOcean-4B, which differ in data, tokenizer, objective and architecture. No version predicts that a differently trained smaller model cannot beat a larger one, so this does not bear on any version. The only same-family size contrast, GenomeOcean 500M vs 4B, is two third-party checkpoints evaluated as baselines on DNA tasks. It shows no scaling trend or predictability, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V5/V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say Generanno (500M) beats GenomeOcean-4B on nearly all tasks, 'defies conventional scaling laws'. They attribute this to functional-sequence training, single-nucleotide tokenization and architecture. Citing ProteinGym (not their experiment), they suggest scaling may plateau in scientific domains. They argue that compact task-specific models are preferable.
record.recipe_differences: No Kaplan or Hoffmann loss-scaling or compute-allocation procedure is used. The study compares task-fine-tuned genomic foundation models and their downstream benchmark scores.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported scores vary by benchmark task. The paper also compares different model families, tokenization and training approaches, so these results do not isolate parameter count as the cause of performance differences.

fits_no_version.finding: GenomeOcean-4B beats GenomeOcean-500M on 14 of 18 Table 2 tasks after full fine-tuning. It is slightly lower, within noise, on pyruvate, arabinose and ammonium. Gains are largest on mixed-marker (0.827 to 0.872) and pH 6 fitness (0.504 to 0.573).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a genomic model family, a larger checkpoint gives small, inconsistent downstream gains after fine-tuning (two sizes only).

fits_no_version.finding: Generanno (500M, functional-sequence data, single-nucleotide tokenizer, MLM) exceeds GenomeOcean-4B on most tasks. The authors call this defying scaling laws.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data curation and tokenization can outweigh an 8x parameter gap across model families on DNA benchmarks.

record.problems: There is no controlled model-size sweep with fixed data, architecture and training recipe, no held-out pretraining-loss measurements, and no fitted scaling curves. Comparisons across model families are confounded by training data, tokenization and architecture. The benchmark includes 10-fold cross-validation standard errors, but those do not resolve the confounds.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3–6 report gene-annotation metrics for Generanno and other annotation tools, but they do not compare parameter scaling in a way that measures V6. Table 7 results other than the pseudogene-classification comparison were omitted to stay within the 60-row limit. Table 8's random-fragment taxonomic classification scores were also omitted after prioritizing the Table 2 benchmark and the Table 7 pseudogene comparison.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute
No shape ablations at fixed parameter count
No power-law fit for DNA models; only two sizes of one third-party family evaluated
No scale sweep or loss-to-downstream relation; only an unmatched cross-family comparison and a two-point GenomeOcean contrast
No exponents or fitting choices examined

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 labels are dropped. The GO500 vs GO4B contrast has only two third-party checkpoints and no loss or trend fit, so it cannot support predictability. The Generanno vs GO4B comparison is confounded by data, tokenizer and objective, and does not test any version. Several GO4B 'reversed' states were differences within standard errors. Table 8 also shows GO4B above GO500 on 3 of 4 taxonomic levels; it does not change the assessment.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; bottleneck conditions and several-orders-of-magnitude power-law behavior.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, and its scaling with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior across modalities or training regimes.

The paper compares downstream scores, but does not measure pretraining loss or establish a predictive relationship between it and downstream performance; model comparisons are not controlled scaling runs.
The paper does not test fitted exponents, compute-optimal allocations, or how fitting choices alter them.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GenomeOcean 500M versus GenomeOcean 4B across the Table 2 benchmark tasks
reader_labels.reason: The 4B model scores higher on most reported tasks, including random-fragment classification; rows T2-GO500-* and T2-GO4B-* show the task-wise comparisons.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparison of Generanno (500M) with GenomeOcean (4B), across the reported tasks
reader_labels.reason: The authors say Generanno surpasses the larger model across nearly all tasks, but this is a comparison across different model families and training setups, not a matched scale sweep; rows T2-GEN-* and T2-GO4B-* document the reported scores.
